name: Banff
blurb: Canada's highest town, founded around hot springs; the Bow River and Cascade Mountain frame its main street.

name: Lake Louise
blurb: Glacial flour from the Victoria Glacier turns it that milky turquoise; the hamlet sits about 4 km downhill.

name: Calgary
blurb: Where the Bow meets the Elbow; on a clear day the Rockies' front ranges line the western skyline 80 km away.

name: Jasper
blurb: Railway town in the Athabasca valley, badly hit by the 2024 wildfire; hub for the Skyline, Tonquin and Edith Cavell.

name: Edmonton
blurb: Alberta's capital straddles the North Saskatchewan River valley, home to North America's largest urban parkland.

name: Moraine Lake
blurb: Sits under the Valley of the Ten Peaks; the rockpile at its outlet is probably a rockslide, not a moraine at all.

name: Canmore
blurb: Former coal-mining town turned climbing and ski-touring base, tucked under the Three Sisters and Ha Ling.

name: Icefields Parkway
blurb: Highway 93N: 232 km from Lake Louise to Jasper, topping out at Bow Summit and passing a hundred-odd glaciers.

name: Athabasca Glacier
blurb: Toe of the Columbia Icefield, visible from the Parkway; it has retreated well over a kilometre since the 1840s.

name: Drumheller
blurb: Badlands town in the Red Deer River valley; hoodoos, dinosaur bones and the Royal Tyrrell Museum.

name: Waterton
blurb: Waterton Park townsite, where prairie slams into mountains; boat to Crypt Lake trailhead leaves from here.

name: Wapta Traverse
blurb: Classic hut-to-hut ski traverse along the Divide: Peyto, Bow, Balfour and Scott Duncan huts, exiting past Sherbrooke Lake.

name: Mount Temple
blurb: At 3,544 m the highest peak in the Lake Louise area; scrambler's route up the SW side, while the north face is a serious alpine test.

name: Mount Columbia
blurb: Highest point in Alberta at 3,747 m, perched on the Divide at the far edge of the Columbia Icefield.

name: Mount Alberta
blurb: First climbed by a Japanese party in 1925, who reportedly left an ice axe on top; still one of the Rockies' hardest summits.

name: Mount Edith Cavell
blurb: Its 1,500 m north face, first climbed in 1961, is one of North America's classic alpine climbs.

name: Castle Mountain
blurb: Crenellated massif over the Bow Valley; Eisenhower Tower anchors its SE end, reached from a popular climbers' hut.

name: Ha Ling Peak
blurb: Named for a Chinese cook who reportedly climbed it on a bet in 1896; Canmore's favourite quick hike.

name: Mount Sir Douglas
blurb: Kananaskis's highest summit at 3,406 m, straddling the Divide, with a glaciated approach over the Haig Glacier.

name: Yamnuska
blurb: Mount John Laurie's limestone south face, the first big wall you see driving west; a cradle of Rockies rock climbing.

name: Lake Agnes Tea House
blurb: Built by the CPR in 1901; everything is hauled up on foot or by helicopter, and there's no electricity.

name: Skyline Trail
blurb: 44 km from Maligne Lake to Maligne Canyon, with about 25 km above treeline over Big Shovel Pass and the Notch.

name: Crypt Lake
blurb: Boat approach, ladder, and a crawl through a rock tunnel lead to this lake right against the US border.

name: Maligne Lake
blurb: Largest natural lake in the Canadian Rockies; Spirit Island is reached by boat from the north end.

name: Portland
blurb: City of bridges at the Willamette-Columbia confluence, with Mt Hood on the eastern skyline.

name: Mount Hood
blurb: Oregon's highest peak at 3,429 m; the south side route via the Hogsback is one of the most-climbed glaciated peaks.

name: Crater Lake
blurb: Collapsed caldera of Mount Mazama, about 7,700 years old; at 594 m it's the deepest lake in the US.

name: Multnomah Falls
blurb: Two-tier falls dropping about 189 m, with the Benson Bridge spanning between the tiers.

name: Eugene
blurb: Track Town USA on the Willamette; the McKenzie River corridor to the Three Sisters starts just east.

name: Salem
blurb: Oregon's capital, midway up the Willamette Valley; Silver Falls and its Trail of Ten Falls lie just east.

name: Astoria
blurb: Oldest US settlement west of the Rockies, at the Columbia's mouth; Lewis and Clark wintered nearby.

name: Smith Rock
blurb: Welded tuff above the Crooked River; Alan Watts' 1986 Chain Reaction helped launch US sport climbing here.

name: Bend
blurb: High-desert outdoor town on the Deschutes, 35 km from Mt Bachelor; Pilot Butte is a cinder cone right in town.

name: Three Sisters
blurb: North, Middle and South Sister, all over 3,000 m; South Sister is a popular walk-up with a crater lake on top.

name: Mount Jefferson
blurb: Oregon's second-highest peak, 3,199 m; its exposed summit pinnacle turns back many parties.

name: Cannon Beach
blurb: Named after a cannon washed ashore from USS Shark in 1846; Haystack Rock towers off the beach.

name: Mount Bachelor
blurb: Young Cascade volcano and big ski area; lifts reach the summit, so skiing 360 degrees off the top is possible.

name: Columbia River Gorge
blurb: The Columbia's cut through the Cascades, carved larger by Ice Age Missoula Floods; windsurfing mecca at Hood River.

name: Broken Top
blurb: Heavily eroded stratovolcano exposing its layered innards; the Crater Ditch and Green Lakes approaches are classics.

name: Three Fingered Jack
blurb: Crumbling volcanic plug; the summit block has a famous exposed step with big air below.

name: Mount Thielsen
blurb: The Lightning Rod of the Cascades; fulgurites coat the needle-like summit pinnacle.

name: Eagle Cap
blurb: Centerpiece of the Wallowas' granite high country; radiating valleys give the wilderness its name.

name: Steens Mountain
blurb: Huge fault-block mountain; the east face drops about 1,500 m to the Alvord Desert, and a gravel road nearly reaches the top.

name: Painted Hills
blurb: John Day Fossil Beds unit whose red, gold and black bands record ancient soils from a warmer climate.

name: Alvord Desert
blurb: Dry lakebed under Steens' east scarp, flat enough for land-speed records; hot springs on the edge.

name: Timberline Trail
blurb: Roughly 66 km loop around Mt Hood via Paradise Park, Ramona Falls, Cairn Basin and Cloud Cap, with unbridged glacial creek fords.

name: Deschutes River
blurb: Rises at Little Lava Lake, loops south through Wickiup, then runs north past Bend and Maupin to the Columbia. Big whitewater.

name: Historic Columbia River Highway
blurb: Opened 1916 as America's first planned scenic highway, looping past Vista House and the waterfalls to The Dalles.
